description: A bare `loadData()` CALL at the immediate body-top of the §40.8 default-logic body fires E-CALL-NOT-IN-LOGIC-CONTEXT. The function IS declared (in the `${ ... }` block above it) — the wrong is the call's SHAPE at that locus, not name resolution. Left bare, the call is emitted as page TEXT and never runs.
rationale: §40.8 S368 amendment (operator ruling `c`, user-voice S368): default-logic mode auto-lifts DECLARATIONS only, and the complement falls through to "emit as text" — right for prose, wrong for logic. A call is a scrml logic form by the identical reasoning that already rejects a bare write (the S123 amendment: "writes ARE logic; logic goes in `${...}`"), so a bare call at the IMMEDIATE body-top of a default-logic body SHALL fire this code. Measured pre-fix: the shape compiled at exit 0 and shipped the literal string into the emitted HTML. The discriminator is scrml's grammar ONLY — operator-ruled in the same breath that "'valid js' is not a consideration one way or another" — so a call is diagnosed because `ident(...)` is a scrml call form, never because a run parses as JS. This case uses the IMPLICIT default-logic body (a file with no `<program>` wrapper), the same locus shape as the `write-not-in-logic-context-pos` sibling.
